messages.subject: Part 1 error
parts:
Dear Dr. van Hees, 

I work at the BC Children's Hospital Research Institute. For one of our studies, we collect 14 days of data using accelerometers (Actigraph GT9X links) during the day (no night sleep data). 

Data is collected in 60 sec epochs at 30 Hz on ActiLife software (firmware 1.7.2) 

According to the vignette, we should be able to process the ActiLife csv files with no time stamps with the package. This didn’t work for us as the files do not appear to be in the format GGIR requires.

The initial work around for this was to use a gt3x file instead. This didn’t work; possibly because the data was collected on firmware version 1.7.2, whereas at the time, GGIR only worked “out of the box” with gt3x on firmware 2.5.0 and later. 

 The second work around was to convert the gt3x file to a csv file in R first and then process this. In R we

  1. Ran standalone version of read_gt3x to convert the gt3x to a matrix.
  2. Converted the matrix to a dataframe to enable the timestamps
  3. Exported the dataframe to a csv file
  4. Ran the R csv through GGIR.

This was unsuccessful as well. After running the script we got this warning:

Warning: number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length Error in which (data[ , 1]== 0 & data[ , 2]==0 & data[ , 3]==0): ‘list’ object cannot be coerced to type ‘double’.

This is where we are stuck. We suspect the problem lies in the gpart.1  and that GGIR cannot read the R csv without timestamps.

Here is the R script we have been using:

To convert to csv:

```{r convert_to_csv,echo=TRUE}

setwd("C:\\Users\\mn.wharton\\Desktop")

gt3x_file<-read.gt3x("101.gt3x")

df<-as.data.frame(gt3x_file)

write.csv(df,"101.csv",row.names = FALSE)

```

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: Part 1 error
parts:
Hi,

Can you check that the accelerometer signal in your csv is stored as a numeric vector?  I think that if you add the argument asDataFrame = TRUE to your read.gt3x function you would get it in the right format.

Best,
Jairo
